name: RF skin-tightening device

lead: A home radiofrequency skin-tightening device uses low-power radio waves delivered through metal electrodes pressed against the face to warm the skin. It is sold for wrinkles, lax skin and a firmer facial contour.
It is a lower-power relative of clinic radiofrequency treatments and is one of the home devices with published randomized data.

paras: Radiofrequency energy heats the dermis, which shrinks existing collagen fibers and prompts fibroblasts to produce new collagen over weeks. Consistent use is needed because each session delivers only mild heating.

Reported effects are mild redness and warmth, with burns possible from overheating or poor contact. Small randomized and open-label trials show modest wrinkle improvement, but wrinkle scores decline again after use stops, and many studies are short and sponsor-linked. Expect subtle tightening, not a facelift.
